s:
Scientist led by PRL Professor discovered new Jupiter size exoplanet in May 2023.
Which of the following statements is/are correct in this context?

I. The mass of this exoplanet is 13 times that of Jupiter.

II. The team was led by professor Abhijit Chakraborty at the exoplanet research group of the physical research laboratory.
x: Both are correct: the exoplanet TOI-4603b found by PRL (May 2023) is about 13 times Jupiter's mass, and the team was led by Prof. Abhijit Chakraborty of PRL's exoplanet group.

s: The National Atmospheric Research Laboratory is located near
x: NARL is at Gadanki, near Tirupati (Andhra Pradesh).

s: MoU was signed between ISRO's Telemetry Tracking and Command Network and which other organisations on August 6, 2017?
x:
Printed key: All of the above (ISRO, DoS, CSIR). Strictly the MoU was between ISTRAC (ISRO/DoS) and CSIR-NPL; ISRO and DoS are ISTRAC's own parents, not 'other organisations'.
In August 2017 ISTRAC of ISRO, Department of Space, signed an MoU with CSIR's National Physical Laboratory (NPL) for time and frequency traceability, so the parties were ISRO, DoS and CSIR (the official date is 4-7 Aug 2017; 6 Aug in the stem).

s: MoU was signed between ISRO's Telemetry Tracking Command Network and which other organisation on August 6, 2017?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (CSIR-National Physical Laboratory); it is added as option 5.
The August 2017 MoU was between ISTRAC (ISRO, Department of Space) and CSIR-National Physical Laboratory, for time and frequency traceability; NASA, ESA and JAXA were not parties, so 'All of the above' (printed key) is wrong.

s: Which Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle was used by ISRO to launch Chandrayaan-2 spacecraft?
x: Chandrayaan-2 went up on GSLV Mk III-M1 (LVM3-M1) on 22 Jul 2019. GSLV Mk IV and Mk V do not exist.

s:
LVM3-M2 successfully placed 36 satellites in orbit. Correct sentences regarding this are

a. This is the first New Space India Ltd. Mission with LVM3.

b. One Web limited is a Network Access Associate.

c. 36 satellites weight - 644 kg.

d. LVM3-M2 weight - 5796 kg.
x: a and b are right: LVM3-M2 (23 Oct 2022) was the first NSIL mission with LVM3, for Network Access Associates Ltd (OneWeb). c and d swap the figures: the 36 satellites weighed 5,796 kg, and the rocket weighs about 640 t.

s: What is the name of the World's smallest Spacecrafts launched into space by PSLV C-38 of ISRO?
x: PSLV-C38 (Jun 2017) carried the 'Sprites', gram-scale chip satellites on the Venta-1 and Max Valier satellites, called the world's smallest spacecraft.

s: Which of the following vehicle successfully launched Chandrayaan-3 into orbit.
x: Chandrayaan-3 was launched on LVM3-M4 on 14 Jul 2023. PSLV-C57 carried Aditya-L1 and PSLV-C48 carried RISAT-2BR1.

s: Kalpana-1 was the first dedicated meteorological satellite launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation using a Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle in which of the following years?
x: METSAT, India's first dedicated weather satellite, was launched by PSLV-C4 on 12 Sep 2002 and renamed Kalpana-1.

s:
Consider the following statements :
1. India launches its first full-fledged meteorological satellite (METSAT) in September, 2002.
2. For the first time, the space vehicle PSLV C-4 carried a payload of more than 1000 kg into a geosynchronous orbit. Which of these statements is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: METSAT (Kalpana-1), India's first full meteorological satellite, was launched on 12 Sep 2002. PSLV-C4 carried it (1,060 kg), the first time a PSLV took over 1,000 kg towards geosynchronous orbit.

s: Which of the following Launch Vehicles launched the Geo Imaging Satellite (GISAT-1) on 5 March 2020 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota?
x: GISAT-1 was assigned to GSLV-F10 for 5 Mar 2020. That launch was postponed; GSLV-F10 finally flew on 12 Aug 2021 and was lost after a cryogenic-stage anomaly.

s: Which of the following vehicle successfully launched the Aditya-L1 mission.
x: Aditya-L1 was launched by PSLV-C57 on 2 Sep 2023. LVM3-M4 carried Chandrayaan-3.

s: How many satellites were launched by ISRO's Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) at Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota in the month of February, 2017?
x: PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites (Cartosat-2 plus 103 co-passengers, 101 of them foreign) from Sriharikota on 15 Feb 2017, a world record at the time.

s: What is the name of the launch vehicle used by Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) for launching NVS-01 navigation satellite into orbit in May 2023?
x: NVS-01 was launched in May 2023 by GSLV-F12. F14 carried INSAT-3DS (2024), F16 carried NISAR (2025), and F18 had not flown.

s: How many times the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) took flights to the space?
x:
the count rises with every launch — now 64 PSLV flights (PSLV-C62, 12 Jan 2026) (app notes 5:35 sub 7)
When this was set, PSLV had flown 16 times; PSLV-C14 (Oceansat-2, Sep 2009) was the 16th flight (now 64 flights, PSLV-C62 in Jan 2026).

s: What is true of the GSLV-F15 mission by ISRO?
o: It marked ISRO's 101 launch from Sriharikota
It marked ISRO's 100th launch from Sriharikota
More than one of the above
x: Both a and c are true: GSLV-F15 carried NVS-02 on 29 Jan 2025, and it was the 100th launch from Sriharikota. b is wrong (100th, not 101st), so 'more than one of the above' is right.

s: Satellites TeLEOS-2 and Lumelite-4 were launched in April 23 from Sriharikota by the launcher :
x: PSLV-C55 launched the Singaporean TeLEOS-2 and Lumelite-4 from Sriharikota on 22 Apr 2023, its 57th mission.

s: In 2017, which Satellite Launch Vehicle of ISRO successfully launched 104 satellites in a single flight?
x: PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites on 15 Feb 2017. INSAT-3DR is a satellite, and PSLV-C55 and GSLV-F12 are 2023 flights.

s: Using a rocket engine made through indigenous technology, ISRO placed 2211 kg INSAT-3DR satellite in orbit in September 2016. The name of the engine is:
x: INSAT-3DR (2,211 kg) went up on GSLV-F05 in Sep 2016 with the indigenous cryogenic (LH2 + LOX) upper stage. The other 'genic' names are not engines.

s: Which rocket was employed in Mangalyaan?
x: Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) was launched by PSLV-C25 in Nov 2013, using orbit-raising burns before Trans-Mars Injection. 'OSLV' does not exist.

s: LVM-3 which is operational since 2022, is associated with which country?
x: LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III) is ISRO's heavy-lift launch vehicle, so it is Indian; France, China and the UK fly Ariane, Long March and no such rocket.

s: Which rocket is called the work horse of ISRO
x: PSLV is called ISRO's 'workhorse' for its reliability and versatility since its first success in 1994. ASLV is retired; GSLV carries heavier GTO payloads; 'RSLV' does not exist.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
s: Which is the heaviest rocket launched by ISRO till date?
x: GSLV Mk III-D1 (5 Jun 2017, ~640 t at lift-off) was the heaviest rocket ISRO had flown when this was asked; the same LVM3 class is still India's heaviest. Mk II and 'Mk I D5' are lighter GSLVs; Mk III-D2 flew only in Nov 2018.

src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Ward Sanitation & Envir
s:
Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding GSLV Mk III?

A. It is a three stage heavy lift launch vehicle developed by ISRO.

B. The first stage uses a liquid propellant and the second stage uses a solid propellant.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
x: The final question asks which is correct. A is correct: GSLV Mk III (LVM3) is a three-stage heavy-lift vehicle. B is wrong: its first stage is solid (S200 strap-ons) and the second liquid (L110), not the reverse.

s:
With reference to India's satellite launch vehicles, consider the following statements:

A. PSLVs launch the satellites useful for Earth resources monitoring whereas GSLVs are designed mainly to launch communication satellites.

B. Satellites launched by PSLV appear to remain permanently fixed in the same position in the sky, as viewed from a particular location on Earth.

C. GSLV Mk III is a four-staged launch vehicle with the first and third stages using solid rocket motors; and the second and fourth stages using liquid rocket engines.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Only A is right: PSLV launches earth-resources satellites to polar/SSO orbits, GSLV mainly communication satellites. B is wrong (fixed-in-sky satellites are geostationary, GSLV's job), and C is wrong (LVM3 has three stages; S-L-S-L is PSLV).

s: What is the approximate weight of the rocket GSLV Mark III D1?
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (About 640 tonnes); it is added as option 5.
GSLV Mk III-D1 weighed about 640 t at lift-off, so none of the printed tonnage options is right. 3-4.5 t is payload scale: its GSAT-19 weighed 3,136 kg, and LVM3 lifts about 4 t to GTO.

src: Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning Asst.
s: Which of the following is not a rocket in operational use by ISRO at present?
x: ASLV was an experimental vehicle, retired after its fourth flight in 1994. GSLV, PSLV and the Rohini sounding rockets are still in use.

s: In February 2023, ISRO carried out the first successful launch using its new ___ rocket.
x: On 10 Feb 2023 SSLV-D2 made the first successful flight of the new Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV-D1 had failed in Aug 2022). GSLV and PSLV are old; Scramjet-TD is not a rocket.

s:
Consider the following statements with reference to " Small satellite launch vehicle " designed by ISRO:
I. It can place a 500 kg payload at a height of 500 km in the Low Earth Orbit (LEO).
II. It has two solid motor stages with a lift off mass of 100 tonnes.
III. It is shorter in length than the PSLV and GSLV.
IV. Unlike the PSLV and GSLV, it can be assembled both vertically and horizontally.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: I, III and IV are correct: SSLV carries 500 kg to 500 km LEO, is shorter (34 m) than PSLV/GSLV and can be assembled vertically or horizontally. II is wrong: it has three solid stages (plus VTM) and ~120 t lift-off mass.

s: Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) launchers have
o: One solid rocket motor stage, one earth storable liquid stage and one cryogenic stage
First and third stage solid rocket motors and second and fourth stage liquid rocket motors
Three liquid stage motors and one solid stage motor
One liquid stage motor and three solid stage motors
x: GSLV has one solid motor stage, one earth-storable liquid (Vikas) stage and one cryogenic upper stage. The S-L-S-L pattern of option b is PSLV.

s:
Which of the following is correct about LVM-3?

I. It is a type of Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle.

II. It launched the Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM).

III. It is configured as a three stage vehicle with two solid strap.
x: I and III are correct: LVM3 is the GSLV Mk III, a three-stage vehicle with two S200 solid strap-ons. II is wrong: the Mars Orbiter Mission flew on PSLV-C25.

s: What is the name of the 'heavy rocket' launched by India in May 2017?
x:
Most keys: GSLV Mk III. Strictly: GSLV Mk III-D1 flew on 5 June 2017, not in May (in May 2017 GSLV-F09 launched the South Asia Satellite).
The 'heavy rocket' of 2017 was GSLV Mk III (D1), widely reported in May 2017 before its launch on 5 Jun 2017. SLV, ASLV and PSLV are small or medium vehicles.

src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-I Panchayat Secretary/Mahil
s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding GSLV Mk III?
o: It is a three stage heavy lift launch vehicle
It can be used to place satellites in Geosynchronous orbit
x: 'Developed by DRDO' is the incorrect statement: ISRO developed GSLV Mk III (LVM3). It is a three-stage heavy-lift vehicle that launched Chandrayaan-2 and can reach GTO.

s:
Which of the following is correct about SSLV developed in 2020?

I. It is a three stage launch vehicle.

II. Its main feature is launch on demand feasibility.
x: Both are correct: SSLV has three solid stages (plus a liquid VTM), and its key feature is low-cost launch on demand.

s: As per the expectations of ISRO, which rocket would be a " game changer " in the operations of ISRO?
x: GSLV Mk III-D1, which launched GSAT-19 in Jun 2017, was hailed as ISRO's 'game changer': it ended dependence on foreign launchers for 4-tonne satellites. D2 came in 2018, and Mk IV does not exist.

s:
PSLV type satellite launching vehicle is used to launch:

A. Remote sensing satellites

B. Interstellar probes

C. Communication satellites

D. Navigation satellites
Choose the correct answer:
x: PSLV has launched remote-sensing (IRS), communication (GSAT-12, CMS-01) and navigation (IRNSS) satellites and the interplanetary Chandrayaan-1 and Mars Orbiter. Only option b contains A, C and D, so 'interstellar' is read loosely as interplanetary.

s: Where was India's first rocket launching station setup?
x: India's first rocket launching station was TERLS at Thumba, near Thiruvananthapuram, where a Nike-Apache flew on 21 Nov 1963. Sriharikota came later for orbital launches.

s: The ISRO conducts 200th consecutive successful launch of RH 200 sounding rocket from :
o: North Eastern Space Applications Centre, Umiam, Meghalaya
x: The RH-200 made its 200th consecutive successful flight from TERLS, Thumba (Thiruvananthapuram) in November 2022, not from Sriharikota.

s: Which of the following is Sounding Rocket of India developed by ISRO?
x: RH-200 is one of ISRO's Rohini sounding rockets. SLV, ASLV and PSLV are orbital satellite launch vehicles.

s:
Which of the following statements is correct about Sounding Rockets of ISRO?

I. ISRO has developed a series of Sounding Rockets called Rohini

II. RH-200, RH-300 and RH-560 are Important Sounding Rockets of ISRO
x: ISRO's sounding rockets form the Rohini series, and RH-200, RH-300 and RH-560 are its operational versions, so both statements are correct.

src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
s: ISRO successfully made the 200th consecutive launch of the multipurpose sounding rocket from Thiruvananthapuram’s Thumba coast in November 2022. What is the name of this sounding rocket?
x: The 200th consecutive successful Thumba launch in Nov 2022 was the RH-200 sounding rocket; the RH number is the diameter in mm. DH, MH and CH-200 do not exist.

s:
India developed the Satellite launch vehicles over a period of few decades. Which is the correct chronological order of development of the following vehicles A, B, C and D ? Select correct answer from Code below :
A. PSLV
B. ASLV
C. SLV
D. GSLV
Code :
x: Order: SLV (first flight 10 Aug 1979) → ASLV (24 Mar 1987) → PSLV (20 Sep 1993) → GSLV (18 Apr 2001), i.e. C, B, A, D.

s:
In the context of the Indian Space Programme undertaken by ISRO, arrange the following events in correct chronological order beginning from the first to the last.

I. Launch of ASTROSAT

II. Launch of the first experimental flight of GSLV MKIII (LVM3-X)

III. Launch of IRNSS-1I
x: LVM3-X/CARE flew on 18 Dec 2014, ASTROSAT was launched on 28 Sep 2015 and IRNSS-1I on 12 Apr 2018, so the order is II-I-III.

s:
Which is the correct chronological sequence of the major events given below?

A. SLV-3 Launch

B. Formation of Bangladesh

C. Sikkim becomes 22nd State of the Indian Union

D. Pokharan-I test
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
x: Bangladesh was formed in Dec 1971, Pokhran-I came in May 1974, Sikkim became the 22nd state in May 1975, and SLV-3 first flew in Aug 1979 (first success Jul 1980): B-D-C-A.

s:
Match the following
Launch Vehicle - Satellite

A. Satellite Launch Vehicle-3 (SLV-3) -
1. Chandrayaan-1

B. Augmented Satellite Launch Vehicle (ASLV) -
2. Rohini

C. Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) -
3. SROSS-C

D. Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) -
4. EDUSAT
Which of the following are correctly matched:
x: SLV-3 launched Rohini (A-2), ASLV SROSS-C (B-3), PSLV Chandrayaan-1 (C-1) and GSLV EDUSAT (D-4).

s: Which of the following company won the contract for next 5 polar satellite launch vehicle (PSLV) in August 2023?
x: NSIL chose the HAL–L&T consortium as the Indian industry partner to build five PSLV-XL rockets end to end (announced 2023).

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening

x: Skyroot's Vikram-S ('Prarambh'), launched on 18 Nov 2022, was India's first private rocket. Agni-V is a DRDO missile, and RLV-TD and SSLV-D1 are ISRO vehicles.

x: Galileo belongs to the European Union, not the USA (whose system is GPS). India-IRNSS, China-BeiDou and Russia-GLONASS are correct.

s: Which one of the following countries has its own Satellite Navigation System?
x: Japan has its own regional system, QZSS (Michibiki). Australia, Canada and Israel have none; the other systems are GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou and NavIC.

s: Which one of the following countries has its own Satellite Navigation System?
x: Japan runs QZSS, one of the two regional systems (with India's NavIC). Australia, Canada and Israel have no satellite navigation system of their own.

s: GPS stands for which one of the following ?
x: GPS = Global Positioning System, the US space-based navigation system, fully operational from 1995.

s: What is the Galileo Project which has been in news recently?
o: An inter-country programme of missile shield
A project developed by India with assistance from
An environmental protection project being developed
A multi-satellite navigation project being developed
x: Galileo is Europe's global multi-satellite navigation system, live since 2016 and under civilian control. It is not a missile shield or an environmental project.

s:
If a major solar storm (solar flare) reaches the Earth, which of the following are the possible effects on the Earth?

A. GPS and navigation systems could fail.

B. Tsunamis could occur at equatorial regions.

C. Power grids could be damaged.

D. Intense auroras could occur over much of the Earth.

E. Forest fires could take place over much of the planet.
F. Orbits of the satellites could be disturbed.
G. Shortwave radio communication of the aircraft flying over polar regions could be interrupted.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: A, B, D and E only
B, C, E, F and G only
A, C, D, F and G only
A, B, C, D, E, F and G
x: Solar storms can make GPS fail, damage power grids, produce intense auroras, disturb satellite orbits and cut shortwave radio on polar flights (A, C, D, F, G). They do not cause tsunamis or forest fires.

src: APPSC Endowment Executive Officer Grade-III Paper-I 2023
s: Which of the following is of great help in monitoring the movement of tectonic plates?
x: GPS (with VLBI and SLR) measures the slow drift of ground stations, so it monitors tectonic plate movement. GIS only analyses maps and WSR-88D is a weather radar.

x: Himachal Pradesh made it mandatory for trekkers to carry a GPS device (June 2019, monsoon-preparedness meeting) so help can reach them in an emergency.

x: IRNSS, NavIC and SBAS are navigation systems, not communication links; APSDMA's real-time satellite communication system is SBMDV (Satellite Based Mobile Data Voice).

In which of the following areas, can GPS technology be used?

I. Mobile phone operations

II. Banking operations

III. Controlling the power grids
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Satellite navigation timing is used in mobile phone networks, banking time-stamps and power-grid synchronisation, so all three apply.

src: Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning Asst.
s: Out of the following, which is one of the systems employed by ISRO for providing Satellite Navigation Services?
x: GAGAN (GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation) is ISRO's satellite navigation (augmentation) service with AAI. INSAT is communication, IRS remote sensing and AstroSat astronomy.

GPS Aided Geo Augmented Navigation (GAGAN) has been developed as a regional Satellite Based Augmentation System (SBAS) by —.

I. Airports Authority of India (AAI)

II. Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO)
x: GAGAN was developed jointly by ISRO and the Airports Authority of India, so both are correct.

s:
Which of the following Agency has the role in development of GPS Aided GEO Augmented Navigation (GAGAN) operational since 2015?

II. Indian Space Research Organisation

III. Defence Research and Development Organisation
x: GAGAN was developed by ISRO and AAI; DRDO had no role.

s: What is Gagan (GAGAN) related to?
o: GPS Aid for Great Air Force and Navy
GPS Aided Great Aviation and Navigation

s:
GPS-Aided Geo Augmented Navigation (GAGAN) uses a system of ground stations to provide necessary augmentation.
Which of the following statements is/ are correct in respect of GAGAN?
I. It is designed to provide additional accuracy and integrity.
II. It will allow more uniform and high quality air traffic management.
III. It will provide benefits only in aviation but not in other modes of transportation.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: GAGAN adds accuracy and integrity (I) and allows uniform, high-quality air traffic management (II). Its benefits also reach maritime, rail and road users, so III is wrong.

s: India's first dedicated navigation satellite IRNSS-1A was launched from :
x: IRNSS-1A was launched by PSLV-C22 on 1 July 2013 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

src: APPSC Dental Asst. Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers,
s: Which atomic clock is used as the Standard of Time in the World?
x: The caesium atomic clock defines the SI second and is the world's time standard. NavIC uses rubidium clocks, which are smaller but slightly less accurate.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
s: What is the reason for failure in the launch of IRNSS-1H satellite of ISRO?
o: The heat shield did not separate
The rocket ran of fuel before the launch
x: IRNSS-1H on PSLV-C39 (31 Aug 2017) failed because the heat shield (payload fairing) did not separate, so the satellite stayed trapped inside.

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about Airborne Laser Terrain Mapping (ALTM)?

I. It is a cheap, fast accurate way of creating 3D digital picture of the earth surface and objects on it.

II. Currently it is mainly used for mapping or survey application
x: Airborne Laser Terrain Mapping is airborne LiDAR: a fast, accurate and cost-effective way to build a 3D digital picture of the ground (I), used today mainly for mapping and survey (II). So both are correct.

s: In the visible spectrum, the colour having the shortest wavelength is :
x: In the visible spectrum violet has the shortest wavelength and red the longest.

s: Which of the following is a popular remote sensing method that used light in the form of a pulsed laser to measure ranges (distances) to a target on Earth's surface?
x: LiDAR (Light Detection And Ranging) uses laser pulses to measure distances and make 3D maps.

s: The rays that deeply darken the photographic plate are:
x: X-rays are highly energetic and strongly expose (darken) photographic plates and film, the basis of radiography; infrared and visible light act weakly. Ultraviolet also affects plates but less deeply.

src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
s: Which of the following radiation/light has longest wavelength among the given options?
x: Wavelength falls from radio through microwave, infrared, visible (red to violet), ultraviolet to X-rays, so infrared is the longest here.

s: Which of the following can be used to capture the heat radiated by volcanic eruptions?
x: Volcanic heat is emitted thermal infrared radiation, so infrared-sensitive sensors capture it; visible or UV sensors record reflected light, not heat.

src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
s: Which of the following band of Electromagnetic Spectrum is best suited for satellite remote sensing of cloud covered disaster affected area, because of its ability to penetrate clouds?
x: Only long-wave microwave/radio energy (as used by SAR) passes through cloud, so 'Radio' is right. Visible, infrared and near-infrared light are blocked by cloud (official key: Visible, a factual error).

s: The colour of light is determined by its
x: The colour of light is set by its wavelength (frequency); red is longest and violet shortest in the visible band.

s: Which of the following is an active sensor used in remote sensing?
x: A laser is an active sensor because it sends its own pulse and reads the echo; visible, infrared and X-ray cameras are passive here.

o: Low Income and Drought Affected Regions
Licensed Development Agency of the Region

B. RISAT is a microwave satellite

x: EOS-03 (earlier GISAT-1) was the geo-imaging satellite for near-real-time flood and cyclone watch; EOS-04 is RISAT-1A, EOS-05 GISAT-1A and EOS-06 Oceansat-3.

x: CNES (Centre National d'Etudes Spatiales) is France's space agency; ISRO and CNES signed the maritime surveillance pact in March 2019.

B. predicting the onset of monsoons

s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Remote Sensing system?
x: The stages are energy source, radiation through the atmosphere, interaction with the target, recording, transmission/reception/processing, interpretation and application. 'Interaction of energy with minimisation' is not one.

s: Which of the following is NOT the application of remote sensing in disaster management?
x: Remote sensing is used for glacial lakes, wildfires and wind/cyclone tracking; 'hills management' is not a disaster application.

s: Remote Sensing uses which of the following in its applications?
x: Remote sensing measures reflected and emitted electromagnetic radiation from a distance; sonar uses sound, not EM waves.

x: Infrared (thermal) cameras detect the body heat of people trapped under rubble even when they cannot be seen.

x: JACIE (Joint Agency Commercial Imagery Evaluation) is a collaboration of US agencies (NASA, NOAA, NGA, USGS, USDA) that use and produce satellite land remote-sensing data; the other options are Indian institutes.

o: A mini satellite launched by ISRO for promoting distance education in India
The name given to the next Moon Impact Probe for Chandrayaan-II
A geoportal of ISRO with 3-D imaging capabilities of India
A space telescope developed by India
x: Bhuvan is ISRO's geoportal with 3-D imaging of India, not a satellite, Moon probe or telescope.

s: As per satellite images released by the National Remote Sensing Centre of the Indian Space Research Organisation, Joshimath in Uttarakhand sank at a pace of ____ cm in 12 days between December 2022 and January 2023.
x: NRSC Cartosat-2S images showed Joshimath sank 5.4 cm in 12 days (27 Dec 2022 - 8 Jan 2023), against about 9 cm over April-November 2022.

s: ____ resolution refers to how often a remote sensing platform can provide coverage of an area.
x: Temporal resolution is how often a satellite revisits (covers) the same area; spatial is the smallest object seen, radiometric the sensitivity to energy differences.

s: A number of 52,785 forest fires were detected using MODIS sensor in forest fire season from November 2020 to June 2021. What is the full form of MODIS?
x: MODIS = Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectro-radiometer, the NASA sensor that detected 52,785 forest fires in 2020-21.

s:
For the measurement/estimation of which of the following are satellite images/ remote sensing data used?

I. Chlorophyll content in the vegetation of a specific location.

II. Greenhouse gas emission from rice paddies of a specific location.

III. Land surface temperature of a specific location.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Satellite data estimate chlorophyll (NDVI), land surface temperature (thermal infrared) and methane/GHG emissions from rice paddies, so all three are correct.

src: APPSC Endowment Executive Officer Grade-III Paper-I 2023
s:
Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI), Satellite Laser Ranging (SLR) and the Global Positioning System (GPS) are most commonly used space-based techniques for monitoring which of the following?

A. Mapping of flood inundations

B. Near real time depiction of cyclone track

C. Movement of tectonic plates
x: VLBI, SLR and GPS are space geodesy techniques that measure millimetre shifts of ground stations, i.e. the movement of tectonic plates; floods and cyclones are mapped by imaging satellites.

s: Which of the following is not a type of remote sensing resolution ?
x: The four resolutions are spatial, spectral, temporal and radiometric; 'chemical' resolution does not exist.

s: An artificial satellite orbiting around the Earth does not fall down. This is so because the attraction of Earth
o: does not exist at such distance
is neutralized by the attraction of the moon
provides the necessary speed for its steady motion
provides the necessary acceleration for its motion
x: Earth's gravity supplies the centripetal acceleration that keeps the satellite curving round the Earth; gravity still exists there and the Moon does not cancel it.

s:
Satellites used for telecommunication relay are kept in a geostationary orbit. A satellite is said to be in such an orbit when:
1. The orbit is geosynchronous.
2. The orbit is circular.
3. The orbit lies in the plane of the Earth's equator.
4. The orbit is at an altitude of 22,236 km. Which is the correct answer using the code given below:
x: A geostationary orbit is geosynchronous, circular and in the equatorial plane (1, 2, 3). Its height is about 35,786 km (22,236 miles), so statement 4 in km is wrong.

s:
The satellite used for telecommunication relay are kept in a geostationary orbit. A satellite is said to be in such an orbit when
1. The orbit is geosynchronous.
2. The orbit is circular.
3. The orbit lies in the plane of the Earth's equator.
4. The orbit is at an altitude of 22,236 km.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
x: A geostationary orbit must be geosynchronous, circular and equatorial; its altitude is about 35,786 km, which is 22,236 miles, not 22,236 km.

s:
Which of the following statements about NISAR are correct?

A. It is an Earth-Observation satellite, jointly developed by the NASA and ISRO

B. It was envisioned by NASA and ISRO eight years ago in 2014.

C. It is expected to be launched in January 2024 from Satish Dhawan Space Centre.

D. It is a High Earth Orbit (HEO) observatory and will operate for a minimum of ten years.
Choose the correct answer:
x:
'expected to be launched in January 2024' — now launched 30 July 2025 on GSLV-F16 from Sriharikota into a sun-synchronous orbit and operational (PMF S&T Part 2 p.56)
A, B and C were correct when asked: NISAR is a NASA-ISRO Earth-observation radar satellite, agreed in 2014, then due from Sriharikota in Jan 2024 (now launched 30 July 2025 on GSLV-F16). D is wrong: it flies in a sun-synchronous low Earth orbit.

src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
s: Which of the following satellite missions, a collaboration between NASA and ISRO, is set to launch in June 2025?
x:
'set to launch in June 2025' — now launched 30 July 2025 on GSLV-F16 and operational (PMF S&T Part 2 p.56)
NISAR is the NASA-ISRO SAR mission (NASA L-band, ISRO S-band); the others are Indian-only satellites. It actually launched on 30 July 2025 on GSLV-F16 (now operational).
